demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors. The shell, in the kit, with PROJECT, REGION, NUMBER, API and tok from the block above. Steps 4 to 7 run offline at Rs 0 and need no project: the first make agent-turn or make agent-eval builds ~/graph-venv with the chat image's pins (lessons 5.4 and 10.1 may have made it already), which takes a few minutes once. Step 3 uses the chat service on your lane; steps 8 and 9 call gemini-3.6-flash and gemini-3.1-flash-lite on location global, and rag-api's /v1/passages as documind-ui-sa. Step 10's ADK planner runs offline in the same venv, and once, optionally, on the chat service after a redeploy. The bench's desk searches by class and drops every passage that has none (services/chat/desk_agent.py, _search()). Lesson 10.1's setup line gave acme's stored rows their classes. If you have not run it, run this now: every chained row is acme's. A second run finds nothing to change. An exit status of 3 means BigQuery deferred a statement, and its last line says to run it again later.

answer, as the Desk shows it (the model's text, then what code writes):
  Last day of notice: 4 December 2026 [1]. Earned leave encashed on exit: 45 days [6]. Gratuity, an estimate: Rs 2,40,000 [12].

  Worked out in code:
  - Last day of notice (NP-03): 2026-10-05 + 60 days = 2026-12-04 (Friday). The days from NP-03 [1]; the acknowledgement date from your message. The desk's count: calendar days, the first being the day after the written acknowledgement. A handbook that counts the days otherwise moves the date.
  - Earned leave encashed on exit (LV-07): min(80, 45) = 45 days. The balance from your message; the cap from LV-07 [6]. Condition: LV-07 bars encashment during probation: this figure holds only once probation is over.
  - Gratuity, an estimate (Code on Social Security, 2020, s.53(1), s.53(2), s.53 Explanation 3, s.53(3)): 7 years 8 months counts as 8 years (a part of a year over six months counts as a year); Rs 52,000 / 26 x 15 x 8 = Rs 2,40,000. The monthly wage from your message; the years from your message; the months from your message. An estimate, not the amount owed: the wages are the monthly rate last drawn as given; a better term in an award, agreement or contract wins (s.53(5)); a forfeiture under s.53(6) is not counted. No ceiling is applied: s.53(3) caps gratuity at an amount the Central Government notifies, which these documents do not hold.

demos.heading: ReWOO: one plan with placeholders, checked and run in waves, offline
demos.purpose: These functions need no framework and no model: agent_patterns.py imports only the standard library and the kit's shared/ at the top, so the shell's own Python runs them. The cell reads the plan the scripted planner writes for chained-exit-e3 and prints what each step waits for and the waves. Then it prints what a refused value stops, four plans check_rewoo() refuses, one placeholder filled, and an extract worker's figure held to its quote twice. Offline, the corpus is ranked in Python, and a wave's searches share one interpreter: three cold searches side by side can outlast a search's budget, 25 seconds by default, and come back failed, as a slow rag-api's would. The kit's own docstring warns of it. RAG_TIMEOUT_S=90, the value the chat service is deployed with, gives them room.

demos.heading: When a plan pays, what each costs, the libraries' forms, and what the kit does not do yet
demos.purpose: The planner is set on the agent after it is built, so the constructor lessons 5.7 and 6.1 show is unchanged: ADK's flow reads root.planner on every model request, and LlmAgent's pydantic config lets the field be assigned (commands/tests/test_adk_planner.py checks both on the pinned ADK). The other half is the answer, which is the text not marked thought: a plan or a line of reasoning never reaches it, and a reply that was all plan says so instead of answering nothing. Offline, at Rs 0: the kit's own ADK brain with the switch on, on a scripted model, with the search stood in. The plan is stored marked as thought, goes back to the model as plain text with the next call, and stays out of the answer.

demos.purpose: Offline, at Rs 0: the kit's own ADK brain with the switch on, on a scripted model, with the search stood in. The plan is stored marked as thought, goes back to the model as plain text with the next call, and stays out of the answer. On your lane the switch needs the chat service's image to carry this kit, so the run starts with a redeploy (Cloud Build, no model call). It then asks the ADK brain the same question with the switch off and on, and takes the switch off again whatever happens. It is optional for you, at most Rs 10 (two turns, each stopped at the chat service's Rs 5); the author's run is below. It shows what the script cannot: whether Gemini still calls retrieve as a function when the instruction asks for tool code under /*ACTION*/, and what a written plan adds to a turn's calls and rupees.

demos.purpose: At lesson end: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors. The pin back is a separate window on purpose: pasted together with the line above, it would put acme straight back on RAG Engine before the lesson began. Leave it until the lesson's last step is done.
